description:
## Why
The operator needs to collapse a fleet into folders without hiding the worker that needs attention, and move workspaces between folders directly in the sidebar. Backlog item: W2.

## Evidence
- c11: `Sources/ContentView.swift:8392-8408,8535-8536` on origin/main (0ff8887e5e) is the SwiftUI WorkspaceSidebar and workspace list. `Sources/ContentView.swift:8572-8576,8598-8638` precomputes activity/unread and carries flagged/suppressed attention into row values.
- Upstream: cmux #4815/#5018 introduced groups. At upstream/main (920ff39ff7), `Sources/SidebarWorkspaceGroupHeaderView.swift` is an Equatable header but doubles as an anchor workspace; `Sources/SidebarWorkspaceGroupContextMenuRunner.swift` and `Sources/SidebarWorkspaceReorderDropView.swift` are interaction references. Follow-up bugs #5253, #8925, #9176, #13688 and #15892 warn against copying the anchor model.
- Research: `upstream-triage/c11-1.0/06-grab-list.md` proposal §3; Fable audit row 4.12; Astra audit rows 4.12/4.12b. BACKLOG.md D17/W2 makes folders core despite the older deferral in `c11-1.0.html` §4; automatic root filing stays cut.

## Scope
In: W1 folder headers with chevron, icon, name, member count and attention badge; collapse/expand, drag to join/leave/reorder, group context menu, six translations and accessibility labels.
Out: anchor-workspace semantics, generated anchor terminals, automatic root filing, automatic naming, AppKit sidebar rewrite, redesigning the attention state machine or Feed (A1-A4), W4 history, Recently Closed and stable tab numbers. W1 owns persistence and CLI; W3 owns integrated scale/sign-off evidence.

## Approach
Project W1's folder records and current per-tab attention into immutable header values. Keep expensive aggregation outside typing-hot row bodies, preserving existing Equatable optimization. Reserve badge/label space so changing counts and hover controls do not shift hit targets. Violet represents any flagged member, including flagged-and-suppressed; the waiting count excludes suppressed tabs, while unread follows the existing notification definition. A collapsed header must retain the flag signal. Specify drop targets and pinned-segment behavior using W1's move core, including empty and collapsed folders. Context menu exposes Rename, Color, Icon, Pin/Unpin, Ungroup and Delete; deletion follows W1's non-destructive membership contract. Use the existing confirmation pattern if any explicitly destructive member-close action is later proposed; it is not required here.

## Acceptance criteria
1. In the real tagged sidebar, create populated and empty folders via W1; every header shows its chevron, icon, name and correct member count. Collapse hides only member rows, and expand restores the same order without starting or closing any terminal.
2. A fixture containing one unsuppressed waiting tab, one suppressed waiting tab, unread notifications and a flagged-and-suppressed tab shows waiting count one and a violet flag. Collapse, then raise/lower flags on hidden members: the visible header updates correctly without requiring expansion. Unread agrees with member notification records; removing the final flag restores the ordinary badge state.
3. Pointer-driven drags cover ungrouped to folder, folder to ungrouped, folder to folder, within-folder reorder, empty/collapsed targets and cancelled/outside drops. Each changes exactly the intended membership/order, obeys W1 pin semantics, and preserves unrelated workspaces and tab identities.
4. Every context-menu action changes the intended folder only. Ungroup/Delete preserves the members and running work; closing the first member never promotes another into a special anchor role.
5. With an unrelated terminal accepting typed input, badge changes do not move controls, hide the active terminal or steal keyboard/app focus. Group updates issued through non-focus CLI commands have the same preservation behavior.
6. New visible and accessibility strings render in English and all six locales; JSON is valid and interpolation tokens are preserved. Long labels and changing counts remain usable at narrow sidebar widths, in Light/Dark theme slots and with keyboard/VoiceOver navigation.

## Validation
Add behavioral attention-projection and drop-planner tests, including the suppressed-flag fixture. Use tests_v2 against a tagged socket for setup/oracles, then fresh-context computer use to drive actual drag/drop, menus, collapse and focus; retain screenshots. W3 repeats at 50+ workspaces and supplies Atin's numbered sign-off script. Compare typing under attention/drop churn against F2 budgets; builds and soaks run on Atlas once F1/C11-216 lands, using the build lock and tagged QA launch. No passing claim based only on socket mutations or source-string tests.

## Dependencies
W1 (C11-259) is required. F1 (C11-216) supplies Atlas builds; F2 supplies baseline/budgets. A1/A3 are adjacent attention changes to coordinate with, not a requirement to rebuild their logic here. W3 (C11-261) consumes the integrated sidebar. The lead links cross-workstream dependencies.

## Risks
Sidebar observation breadth and per-member aggregation can regress typing/main-thread responsiveness. Do not add work to hitTest outside pointer handling or forceRefresh. Pin/drop ambiguity and collapse can hide attention unless the explicit fixture passes. No tenant config writes. Six-locale localization and accessible fixed geometry are part of delivery. Sanitize public screenshots, names and paths.

Size: L. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: a visible folder primitive and projection of existing attention; no task inference, auto-answering or agent configuration writes.
title: Workspace groups: sidebar folders, drag/drop and visible attention
